'''Pavel Nedvěd''' ({{IPA|cs|ˈpavɛl ˈnɛdvjɛt|-|Cs-Pavel Nedved.ogg}}; born 30 August 1972) is a Czech former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]]. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest Czech players of all time.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pavel Nedvěd|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/teams/czech_rep/squad/741685.stm|website=BBC News|publisher=BBC|access-date=21 September 2014|archive-date=6 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306183848/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/teams/czech_rep/squad/741685.stm|url-status=live}}</ref>

Nedvěd won numerous trophies with Italian clubs [[SS Lazio|Lazio]] and [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], including the last ever [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|Cup Winners' Cup]] with Lazio. He also led Juventus to the [[2003 UEFA Champions League final]].

Nedvěd was a vital player in the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech]] team that reached the final of [[UEFA Euro 1996|Euro 1996]], after which he attracted the attention of big European clubs. He also captained the team at [[UEFA Euro 2004]], where they were defeated in the semi-final by eventual champions [[Greece national football team|Greece]], and where Nedvěd was named in the Team of the Tournament. He helped his team qualify for the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] for the first time since the breakup of Czechoslovakia. Due to his quick and energetic runs during matches, Nedvěd was nicknamed "''{{lang|it|Furia Ceca}}''" ({{Lit|Czech Fury}}) by Italian football fans. His nickname in Czech is ''Méďa''<ref>{{cite web|title=Pavel "Méďa" Nedvěd vydává v Itálii svou autobiografii|url=http://sport.tn.nova.cz/clanek/sport/fotbal/dalsi-fotbal/pavel-meda-nedved-vydava-v-italii-svou-autobiografii.html|publisher=[[TV Nova (Czech Republic)|TV Nova]]|access-date=11 August 2017|language=cs|archive-date=29 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190629152224/https://sport.tn.nova.cz/clanek/sport/fotbal/dalsi-fotbal/pavel-meda-nedved-vydava-v-italii-svou-autobiografii.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> ({{Lit|Little Bear}}), stemming from the similarity between his surname and the Czech word for bear, ''medvěd''.

Nedvěd won the [[Ballon d'Or]] in 2003, becoming the second Czech player to win the award after [[Josef Masopust]], and the first since the breakup of Czechoslovakia. During his career, Nedvěd received many other individual awards, including the second [[Golden Foot]] award for best footballer worldwide in 2004; the [[Football Association of the Czech Republic|Czech Football Association]]'s [[Czech Footballer of the Year]] four times; and the Czech Sports Journalists' [[Golden Ball (Czech Republic)|Golden Ball]] for best Czech footballer six times. He was also named by [[Pelé]] as one of the [[FIFA 100]] and was named in the [[UEFA Team of the Year]] in 2003, 2004, and 2005. Nedvěd retired from professional football after the [[2008–09 Serie A|2008–09]] season. Nedvěd played 501 league matches at club level, scoring 110 goals, and was [[Cap (sport)|capped]] 91 times for the Czech Republic, scoring 18 goals.

== Club career ==

=== Škoda Plzeň and Dukla Prague loan spell ===
Born on 30 August 1972 in [[Cheb]] and raised in nearby [[Skalná]],<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9j1wbp2t1usC&pg=PA184|title=Historical Dictionary of Soccer|last=Dunmore|first=Tom|date=2011|publisher=Scarecrow Press|isbn=9780810871885|pages=184}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pavelnedved.cz/biografie-2_1.html|title=Pavel Nedvěd: biography|language=cs|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081220172742/http://www.pavelnedved.cz/biografie-2_1.html|archive-date=20 December 2008}}</ref> Nedvěd began his football career in his native Czechoslovakia. A football fan from an early age, he began playing for his hometown club Tatran Skalná in 1977 at the age of five.<ref name=Nedved>{{cite web|title=Pavel Nedvěd|url=http://www.pavelnedved.cz/|access-date=8 June 2011|language=cs|archive-date=2 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130602090557/http://www.pavelnedved.cz/home/|url-status=live}}</ref> Nedvěd moved on to [[FK Hvězda Cheb|Rudá Hvězda Cheb]] in 1985, playing one season before spending five years with [[FC Viktoria Plzeň|Škoda Plzeň]].<ref name="Nedved" /> In 1990, Nedvěd was loaned to [[Dukla Prague]], a club run by the [[Czechoslovak Army|Army]], as part of his [[military service]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Síň slávy Dukla Praha 1948 - 2009: Pavel Nedvěd|trans-title=Hall of fame Dukla Prague 1948–2009: Pavel Nedvěd|url=http://fkdukla.cz/legendy.asp?legenda=64|language=cs|publisher=FK Dukla Prague|access-date=6 October 2015|archive-date=9 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160309070918/http://fkdukla.cz/legendy.asp?legenda=64|url-status=live}}</ref> During his first year at Dukla Prague, he played for {{ill|VTJ Dukla Tábor|cs|VTJ Tábor (fotbal)}}, a lower division club also operated by the Army. On 28 October 1991, Nedvěd played his first match for Dukla Prague.<ref name="konec" /> He played one season for Dukla in 1991 before finishing his military service, thus ending his loan from Plzeň. He later transferred to [[AC Sparta Prague|Sparta Prague]] in 1992.<ref name=jerabek>{{cite book |last=Jeřábek|first=Luboš|title=Český a československý fotbal – lexikon osobností a klubů|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4ErKtwjzyv8C&q=%22Ne%C4%8Das%2C+Radim%22&pg=PA132|access-date=18 March 2012|year=2007|publisher=Grada Publishing|location=Prague|language=cs|isbn=978-80-247-1656-5|page=132}}</ref> Plzeň was about to receive 30% of the transfer fee if Nedvěd transferred to a foreign club.<ref name="kosice1">{{cite news|last=Kellner|first=Tomáš|url=http://www.praguepost.cz/archivescontent/24100-plzen-battles-sparta-praha-off-the-pitch.html|title=Plzen battles Sparta Praha off the pitch|work=[[The Prague Post]]|date=17 July 1996|access-date=8 October 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208060704/http://www.praguepost.cz/archivescontent/24100-plzen-battles-sparta-praha-off-the-pitch.html|archive-date=8 December 2015}}</ref><ref name="kosice2">{{cite news|last=Bouc|first=František|url=http://www.praguepost.cz/archivescontent/25853-soccer-club-incensed-over-cmfs-ruling.html|title=Soccer club incensed over CMFS ruling|work=[[The Prague Post]]|date=30 April 1997|access-date=8 October 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304190615/http://www.praguepost.cz/archivescontent/25853-soccer-club-incensed-over-cmfs-ruling.html|archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref>

===Sparta Prague===
Early in his career at Sparta, Nedvěd was sent off three times in just six matches.<ref name="konec">{{cite news |first=Miroslav |last=Novák |title=Nedvěd: od prvního zápasu k poslednímu. Přijde opravdu konec? |url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/nedved-od-prvniho-zapasu-k-poslednimu-prijde-opravdu-konec-po3-/fot_zahranici.aspx?c=A090528_171752_fot_zahranici_min |newspaper=[[iDNES]] |date=29 May 2009 |access-date=6 October 2015 |language=cs |archive-date=26 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170926235401/https://fotbal.idnes.cz/nedved-od-prvniho-zapasu-k-poslednimu-prijde-opravdu-konec-po3-/fot_zahranici.aspx?c=A090528_171752_fot_zahranici_min |url-status=live }}</ref> With Sparta, Nedvěd won one [[Czechoslovak First League]] title, two [[Gambrinus liga]] titles and a [[Czech Cup]].<ref name=jerabek/> In 1994, he received his first call up to the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic national team]]. His performance at [[UEFA Euro 1996]], including a goal in the group stage against [[Italy national football team|Italy]], attracted attention; despite a verbal agreement with [[PSV Eindhoven|PSV]],<ref name="kosice1" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Afketsen transfer Nedved grootste teleurstelling|work=PSV |trans-title=Ricochet transfer Nedved biggest disappointment|url=http://www.psv.nl/web/show/id=118705/langid=43/contentid=5959|language=nl|publisher=PSV Eindhoven|date=26 March 2004|access-date=8 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203005247/http://www.psv.nl/web/show/id=118705/langid=43/contentid=5959|archive-date=3 December 2013}}</ref> Nedvěd moved from Sparta Prague to Italian [[Serie A]] club [[SS Lazio|Lazio]]. Sparta first sold Nedvěd to Slovak club [[1. FC Košice]], which had the same owner as Sparta, for a 1.5 million [[Czech koruna|CZK]] transfer fee. Immediately, Košice sold Nedvěd to Lazio.<ref name="kosice1" /> Thus Sparta paid only a small fraction of the transfer fee to Plzeň.<ref name="kosice1" /><ref name="skandaly">{{Cite news |title=Skandály a zkraty fotbalového krále Pavla Nedvěda! |url=http://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/svet-hvezd-skandaly/79852/skandaly-a-zkraty-fotbaloveho-krale-pavla-nedveda.html |newspaper=[[Blesk]] |publisher=Czech News Center |date=29 April 2009 |access-date=7 October 2015 |language=cs |archive-date=29 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190629132040/https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/svet-hvezd-skandaly/79852/skandaly-a-zkraty-fotbaloveho-krale-pavla-nedveda.html |url-status=live }}</ref> After Plzeň's protest, the [[Football Association of the Czech Republic|Czech football association]] ordered Sparta to pay Plzeň 35 million CZK in compensation.<ref name="kosice2" />

Nedvěd signed a four-year contract for a fee of [[Italian lira|₤]]1.2 million.<ref>{{cite news |first=Giancarla |last=Ghisi |title=Nedvěd alla Lazio, Bierhoff viaggia verso Torino |url=http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/1996/luglio/11/Nedved_alla_Lazio_Bierhoff_viaggia_co_0_9607113572.shtml |newspaper=[[Corriere della Sera]] |date=11 July 1996 |access-date=17 August 2014 |language=it |archive-date=29 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151129024913/http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/1996/luglio/11/Nedved_alla_Lazio_Bierhoff_viaggia_co_0_9607113572.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref>

Nedvěd played [[UEFA Champions League]] football with Lazio, scoring against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in a 2–2 draw in the second group stage<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-70768275.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130614235836/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-70768275.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=14 June 2013|title=Madrid end Lazio dream; CHAMPIONS LEAGUE ROUND-UP|newspaper=[[Birmingham Evening Mail]]|date=22 February 2001|via=HighBeam Research|url-access=subscription|location=England|access-date=12 January 2013}}</ref> before the Italian side was eliminated. In Lazio's final Champions League match of the season, Nedvěd was criticised by [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] manager [[David O'Leary]] for a challenge on [[Alan Maybury]] (although the referee did not call a foul),<ref>{{cite news|last=Shaw|first=Phil|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-5136392.html|title=Football: Mihajlović dampens the party for Leeds; Leeds United 3 Lazio 3 – Yugoslav international's stoppage-time free-kick denies O'Leary's tenacious reserves a deserved victory over Lazio|newspaper=[[The Independent]]|date=15 March 2001|access-date=12 January 2013|url-status=usurped|via=HighBeam Research|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130603132935/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-5136392.html|location=London, England|archive-date=3 June 2013}}</ref> and he received a three-match suspension from European competitions from [[UEFA]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Tynan|first=Gordon|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-5138068.html|title=Football: Greeks deny meddling charge|newspaper=[[The Independent]]|date=22 March 2001|access-date=12 January 2013|url-status=usurped|via=HighBeam Research|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130604004532/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-5138068.html|location=London, England|archive-date=4 June 2013}}</ref>

Despite Nedvěd's signing a new four-year contract with Lazio in April 2001, the club tried to sell him and teammate [[Juan Sebastián Verón]] that summer, triggering fan protests against club chairman Sergio Cragnotti.<ref>{{cite news|last=Anderson|first=David|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-23856251.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130603130551/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-23856251.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=3 June 2013|title=#23m Verón move expected next week; football news|newspaper=[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]]|date=6 July 2001|via=HighBeam Research|url-access=subscription|access-date=12 January 2013}}</ref> The players were ultimately sold to Juventus and Manchester United respectively.

=== Juventus ===
[[File:Football against poverty 2014 - Zidane et Nedved.jpg|thumb|right|upright=0.9|Nedvěd ''(left)'' was signed by [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in 2001 to replace [[Zinedine Zidane]].]]
After five seasons with Lazio, Nedvěd was speculatively linked to several clubs (including Manchester United and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]])<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/1341352.stm|title=Nedvěd targets United switch|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=20 May 2001|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-date=27 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160227015040/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/1341352.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> before moving to Juventus in July 2001 for 75&nbsp;[[1,000,000,000|billion]]&nbsp;[[Italian lira|lire]] (€38.7&nbsp;million by fixed exchange rate).<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www2.raisport.rai.it/news/rubriche/cmercato/200107/05/3b449bd903662/|title=Nedvěd: "La Juve l'ho scelta io"|date=5 July 2001|access-date=24 September 2017|website=[[Rai Sport]]|publisher=[[RAI]]|language=it|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170925035326/http://www2.raisport.rai.it/news/rubriche/cmercato/200107/05/3b449bd903662/|archive-date=25 September 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2001/giugno/14/Ciao_Juve_Nedved_resta_alla_ga_0_0106144208.shtml|title=Ciao Juve: Nedvěd resta alla Lazio|date=14 June 2001|access-date=24 September 2017|newspaper=[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]|publisher=RCS MediaGroup|location=Milan|language=it|archive-date=29 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190629223934/http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2001/giugno/14/Ciao_Juve_Nedved_resta_alla_ga_0_0106144208.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.sslazio.it:80/news/visualizza_news.asp?idnews=325&titolo=1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010721035749/http://www.sslazio.it/news/visualizza_news.asp?idnews=325&titolo=1|archive-date=21 July 2001|title=Depositati i contratti di cessione di Nedvěd e Verón|date=18 July 2001|access-date=24 September 2017|publisher=SS Lazio|location=Rome|language=it|url-status=dead}}</ref> At Juventus, he replaced [[Zinedine Zidane]], who had transferred to Real Madrid that summer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/news/newsid=1064964.html|title=Nedved: I can retire happy|publisher=FIFA|date=1 June 2009|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130923083602/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/news/newsid=1064964.html|archive-date=23 September 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> Nedvěd was a regular on Juventus' 2001–02 and 2002–03 ''[[List of Italian football champions|Scudetto]]''-winning teams.<ref name=NFTprofile>{{NFT player|id=1853|access-date=3 June 2013}}</ref> Although he was a substantial part of the club's championship season in 2003, he was also the subject of controversy. Nedvěd quit the [[Italian Footballers' Association]] in protest of the union's limit on non-[[European Union]] (EU) players;<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/european/2398119/Nedved-at-double-for-Juventus.html# |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140308033245/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/european/2398119/Nedved-at-double-for-Juventus.html |archive-date=8 March 2014 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Nedvěd at double for Juventus|newspaper=The Daily Telegraph|date=17 March 2003|access-date=31 December 2012}}</ref> his native Czech Republic did not become an EU member until 2004.<ref name="Europa History 00">{{cite web|title=A decade of further expansion|publisher=Europa web portal|url=http://europa.eu/abc/history/2000_today/index_en.htm|access-date=25 June 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070615031714/http://europa.eu/abc/history/2000_today/index_en.htm|archive-date=15 June 2007}}</ref> Nedvěd perfectly led Juventus to the [[2003 UEFA Champions League Final|2003 UEFA Champions League final]] against [[AC Milan|Milan]],<ref name=stay2006>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/5195000.stm|title=Nedvěd decides to stay with Juve|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=27 July 2006|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-date=12 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131012032758/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/5195000.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> but had to sit out the final due to an accumulation of [[Penalty card#Yellow card|yellow cards]] after his semi-final booking for a foul on Real Madrid midfielder [[Steve McManaman]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Nakrani|first=Sachin|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/apr/25/chelsea-champions-league-suspensions|title=Nine other players who have missed major finals due to two bookings|newspaper=The Guardian|date=25 April 2012|access-date=3 April 2015|archive-date=21 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230121221228/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/apr/25/chelsea-champions-league-suspensions|url-status=live}}</ref>

In December 2003, Nedvěd was named World Footballer of the Year by ''[[World Soccer (magazine)|World Soccer]]'' magazine.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/3310291.stm|title=Nedved scoops top award|publisher=BBC Sport|date=11 December 2003|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-date=4 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190704190032/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/3310291.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> Later that month, he won the [[Ballon d'Or|European Footballer of the Year]] award over [[Thierry Henry]] and [[Paolo Maldini]], the second Czech to win the award after [[Josef Masopust]] in 1962.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/3341645.stm|title=Nedvěd scoops top award|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=22 December 2003|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-date=7 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190707130425/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/3341645.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> Nedvěd received further recognition in his home country when he won the 2004 Golden Ball, awarded by Czech sportswriters, for the fifth time in seven years.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/czech_rep/3775871.stm|title=Nedvěd voted Czech's best|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=4 June 2004|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-date=14 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190714082835/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/czech_rep/3775871.stm|url-status=live}}</ref>

The 2004–05 season was frustrating for Nedvěd, who was sidelined for two months by knee and head injuries<ref name=guardian-april2005>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/apr/05/newsstory.sport9|title=Nedvěd threatens to retire|newspaper=The Guardian|date=5 April 2005|access-date=3 April 2015|archive-date=24 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221024022316/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/apr/05/newsstory.sport9|url-status=live}}</ref> and first considered retirement in April 2005.<ref name=guardian-april2005/> Although Juventus won Serie A titles that year and in 2006, the titles were revoked after the ''[[2006 Italian football scandal|Calciopoli]]'' [[match fixing]] scandal. After the 2005–06 season, which ended with Juventus' relegation from Serie A despite its first-place finish,<ref name="Serie A appeals">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/5215178.stm|title=Punishments cut for Italian clubs|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=25 July 2006|access-date=30 July 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060822214348/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/5215178.stm|archive-date=22 August 2006|url-status=live}}</ref> many stars (such as [[Fabio Cannavaro]] and [[Lilian Thuram]]) left the club and the remaining players' future was uncertain.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/5220184.stm|title=Duo to stay at Juve – Deschamps|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=27 July 2006|access-date=14 January 2013|archive-date=9 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190709172539/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/5220184.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> After the 2006 World Cup, Nedvěd dispelled rumours about his departure by reiterating his desire to help Juventus regain promotion to Serie A, citing his family and his commitment to the club as reasons for his decision.<ref name=stay2006/> He received a five-match ban after a red card against [[Genoa CFC|Genoa]] in December 2006,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2006/SPORT/football/12/05/italy.nedved/index.html|title=Protest earns Nedved five-game ban|publisher=[[CNN]]|date=5 December 2006|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304205532/http://edition.cnn.com/2006/SPORT/football/12/05/italy.nedved/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> and repeated his threat to retire.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Nedvěda trest naštval. Můžu skončit, říká|trans-title=Nedvěd upset by punishment. He says he could quit|url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/nedveda-trest-nastval-muzu-skoncit-rika-fde-/fot_zahranici.aspx?c=A061206_134251_fot_zahranici_min|newspaper=[[Mladá fronta Dnes]]|location=Prague|publisher=[[Mafra (company)|Mafra]]|date=6 December 2006|access-date=31 December 2012|language=cs|archive-date=10 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010160339/https://fotbal.idnes.cz/nedveda-trest-nastval-muzu-skoncit-rika-fde-/fot_zahranici.aspx?c=A061206_134251_fot_zahranici_min|url-status=live}}</ref> However, he remained with the club until the end of the season and scored 11 league goals in the [[2006–07 Serie B]].<ref name=NFTprofile/>

[[File:Nedved vs Chinese Olympic Team.jpg|thumb|alt=Two players vying for the ball, with a linesman nearby|Nedvěd playing for Juventus in training, July 2007]]
For the 2007–08 season, Juventus again played in Serie A. Nedvěd played frequently for the ''Bianconeri'', contributing as the team's first-choice left winger and scoring two goals that season. He was again controversial: in November 2007, his tackle of [[Inter Milan]] midfielder [[Luís Figo]] broke Figo's [[fibula]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Nedved apologises over Figo tackle|url=https://int.soccerway.com/news/2007/November/6/nedved-apologises-over-figo-tackle|website=Soccerway|publisher=Platform Group|date=6 November 2007|access-date=20 February 2018|archive-date=21 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230121221222/https://int.soccerway.com/news/2007/November/6/nedved-apologises-over-figo-tackle|url-status=live}}</ref> In April 2008, Nedvěd was hospitalised overnight for a concussion sustained in a collision with [[Roberto Guana]] during a match against [[U.S. Città di Palermo|Palermo]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/nedved-po-otresu-mozku-uz-muze-z-nemocnice-fjx-/fot_zahranici.aspx?c=A080407_134350_fot_zahranici_ot|title=Nedvěd po otřesu mozku už může z nemocnice|trans-title=Nedvěd after concussion can already leave hospital|newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|location=Prague|publisher=Mafra|date=7 April 2008|access-date=31 December 2012|language=cs|archive-date=13 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171213034752/https://fotbal.idnes.cz/nedved-po-otresu-mozku-uz-muze-z-nemocnice-fjx-/fot_zahranici.aspx?c=A080407_134350_fot_zahranici_ot|url-status=live}}</ref>

Nedvěd scored Juventus' first league goal of the 2008–09 season in a 1–1 away draw with [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]],<ref name=0809season>{{cite web|title=Italy 2008–09|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesi/ital09.html|publisher=RSSSF|access-date=3 June 2013|archive-date=21 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230221055148/https://www.rsssf.org/tablesi/ital09.html|url-status=live}}</ref> and scored twice against Bologna in a 2–1 away win in October.<ref name=0809season/> On 26 February 2009, Nedvěd announced he would retire at the end of 2008–09 season<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7912535.stm|title=Juve star Nedved to quit football|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=26 February 2009|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-date=11 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190711171602/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7912535.stm|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.google.com/hostednews/canadianpress/article/ALeqM5iwGFn-OjURYdAh5GQXB0aTUp9fAA| title=Juventus midfielder Pavel Nedvěd to retire at end of the season| agency=The Canadian Press| date=26 February 2009| access-date=26 February 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090303024713/https://www.google.com/hostednews/canadianpress/article/ALeqM5iwGFn-OjURYdAh5GQXB0aTUp9fAA|archive-date=3 March 2009}}</ref> to spend more time with his family.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1032724.html#nedved+announces+retirement|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090303053306/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1032724.html#nedved+announces+retirement|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 March 2009|title=Nedved announces retirement|publisher=FIFA|date=26 February 2009|access-date=31 December 2012}}</ref> On 10 March 2009, he came off as a substitute due to injury after 12 minutes of the Champions League round of 16 second leg match against Chelsea.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7899606.stm|title=Juventus 2–2 Chelsea (agg 2–3)|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=10 March 2009|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-date=9 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190709175250/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7899606.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> Due to his impending retirement and his club's 3–2 loss on aggregate, it was his last European match for Juventus. Nedvěd retired at the end of the season, captaining the final match against his former team Lazio and setting up [[Vincenzo Iaquinta]]'s goal for a 2–0 victory.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/SerieA/Juventus/31-05-2009/juventus-seconda-50472258025.shtml|title=Juventus seconda E Nedved saluta|newspaper=La Gazzetta dello Sport|date=31 May 2009|access-date=31 December 2012|language=it|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090605072405/http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/SerieA/Juventus/31-05-2009/juventus-seconda-50472258025.shtml|archive-date=5 June 2009}}</ref> As of April 2024, Nedvěd has made the most appearances for the Turin side as a non–Italian player (327).<ref>{{Cite web|first=Montavio|last=Says|title=Alex Sandro 3 games away from all-time Juventus record for foreign players|url=https://football-italia.net/alex-sandro-3-away-from-juventus-record/|website=Football Italia|date=3 April 2024|access-date=4 April 2024|archive-date=3 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240403154445/https://football-italia.net/alex-sandro-3-away-from-juventus-record/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== FK Skalná ===
On 23 September 2017, Nedvěd transferred to FK Skalná, based in his native village of [[Skalná]]. The club plays in the 1. B class of in the [[Karlovy Vary Region]] (7th level of Czech football hierarchy).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.irozhlas.cz/sport/fotbal/drzitel-zlateho-mice-v-i-b-tride-pavel-nedve-prestoupil-do-skalne-u-chebu_1709230837_vman|title=Držitel Zlatého míče v I. B třídě. Pavel Nedvěd přestoupil do Skalné u Chebu|work=Czech Radio|access-date=3 June 2018|language=cs|archive-date=21 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221021093000/https://www.irozhlas.cz/sport/fotbal/drzitel-zlateho-mice-v-i-b-tride-pavel-nedve-prestoupil-do-skalne-u-chebu_1709230837_vman|url-status=live}}</ref> Chairman of the club had said: "It was Pavel's dream to play with his son and now it will come true". He further added that it seems likely that his planned fielding on 2 June 2018 in a home fixture against TJ Baník Královské Poříči B is a one-off event, due to Nědved's residency in Italy and employment as vice-president of [[Juventus FC|Juventus]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pavel Nedvěd přestoupil, ve Skalné si splní sen. Zahraje si se synem|url=https://fotbal.idnes.cz/pavel-nedved-skalna-navrat-d0p-/fot_dsouteze.aspx?c=A180511_400629_fot_dsouteze_ten|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|publisher=Mafra|date=11 May 2018|access-date=3 June 2018|language=cs|archive-date=21 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230221055238/https://fotbal.idnes.cz/pavel-nedved-skalna-navrat-d0p-/fot_dsouteze.aspx?c=A180511_400629_fot_dsouteze_ten|url-status=live}}</ref> Nedvěd was in the starting line-up, but Skalná lost the home fixture 1–4, and neither Nedvěd nor his son scored a goal.

==International career==
Nedvěd began playing for Czechoslovakia national youth teams in 1988, representing his country in the under-15 age group before progressing to 16, 17 and 18.<ref name=jerabek/> In 1992, he debuted for the [[Czechoslovakia national under-21 football team|under-21 team]], playing seven times between 1992 and 1993.<ref name=jerabek/>

Nedvěd debuted for the reformed [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic national team]] in June 1994 in a 3–1 victory over the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]].<ref>{{Cite news|first=Vojtěch|last=Šelong|title=Pavel Nedvěd byl světovou hvězdou, za svůj milovaný Juventus však dobojoval|url=https://www.sport.cz/clanek/fotbal-pavel-nedved-zivotopis-1867100|website=[[Seznam.cz]]|date=14 March 2023|access-date=7 September 2024|language=cs|archive-date=7 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240907112922/https://www.sport.cz/clanek/fotbal-pavel-nedved-zivotopis-1867100|url-status=live}}</ref> His first major tournament was Euro 1996, where he scored his first senior international goal and helped his team reach [[UEFA Euro 1996 final|the final]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Czech Republic: The Golden Run in the 1996 European Championship|url=https://breakingthelines.com/historical-series/czech-republic-the-golden-run-in-the-1996-european-championship/|website=Breaking The Lines|date=16 June 2024|access-date=7 September 2024|language=cs|archive-date=7 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240907112923/https://breakingthelines.com/historical-series/czech-republic-the-golden-run-in-the-1996-european-championship/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Euro 1996===
The Czech Republic were not expected to make an impact against the favoured [[Germany national football team|Germany]] side in their opening match; Nedvěd missed two scoring chances and was one of ten players to receive a yellow card as Germany won 2–0.<ref name=czge1996>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0253-0d7b3033bb5b-f5a484e35b4f-1000--germany-overcome-slow-starting-czech-republic-in-euro-96-gr/ |title=Germany overcome slow-starting Czechs|publisher=UEFA|date=6 October 2003|access-date=12 January 2013|url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130112163914/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=1996/matches/round=227/match=52506/postmatch/report/index.html|archive-date=12 January 2013}}</ref> However, he contributed defensively, clearing a goal-bound shot from [[Christian Ziege]] off the [[Association football pitch#Pitch boundary|line]].<ref name=czge1996/>

Nedvěd scored his first senior international goal in his nation's Group C match against Italy, putting the Czech Republic in the lead 1–0 after four minutes.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Jan|last=Palička|title=Den, kdy si Nedvěd připadal jako v nebi. Jak Češi ztrapnili hvězdy z Itálie|trans-title=The day when Nedvěd felt like he was in heaven. How the Czechs embarrassed the stars from Italy|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/euro-2021/serial-tenkrat-v-anglii-cesko-italie-pavel-nedved.A210614_144935_euro-2020_par|newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=14 June 2021|access-date=7 September 2024|language=cs|archive-date=7 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240907112922/https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/euro-2021/serial-tenkrat-v-anglii-cesko-italie-pavel-nedved.A210614_144935_euro-2020_par|url-status=live}}</ref> Although Italy scored an equaliser during the first half, they were reduced to ten men and the Czech Republic scored again before half-time for a 2–1 victory.<ref name=czit1996>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0253-0d7b3025ac77-2c440d520967-1000--bejbl-completes-italian-job-for-czechs-in-euro-96-group-c/ |title=Bejbl completes Italian job for Czechs|publisher=UEFA|date=6 October 2003|access-date=12 January 2013|url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130112160412/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=1996/matches/round=227/match=52508/postmatch/report/index.html|archive-date=12 January 2013}}</ref> Nedvěd played in the third group match, against [[Russia national football team|Russia]], receiving his second yellow card of the tournament as the Czechs tied 3–3 to advance to the knockout stage.<ref name=rucz1996>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0254-0d7b2e487dfe-c5b93767e48f-1000--late-smicer-strike-against-russia-sends-czech-republic-thr/|url-status=live|title=Late Šmicer strike sends Czechs through|publisher=UEFA|date=6 October 2003|access-date=4 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120418142834/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=1996/matches/round=227/match=52510/postmatch/report/index.html|archive-date=18 April 2012}}</ref>

Due to a suspension, Nedvěd missed the Czech Republic's quarter-final match against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/team-news-for-today-s-quarterfinals-1338405.html|title=Team news for today's quarter-finals|newspaper=[[The Independent]]|date=22 June 1996|access-date=12 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231212180537/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/team-news-for-today-s-quarterfinals-1338405.html|archive-date=12 December 2023}}</ref> The Czechs won in his absence and progressed.<ref name=czpt1996>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/match/52914--czechia-vs-portugal/ |title=Poborský lob puts Czechs into semi-finals|publisher=UEFA|date=6 October 2003|access-date=4 June 2013|url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120618200318/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=1996/matches/round=223/match=52914/index.html|archive-date=18 June 2012}}</ref> In the semi-final against [[France national football team|France]], Nedvěd was named [[man of the match]] as the Czech Republic advanced to the final after a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot–out]],<ref>{{Cite news|last=Shaw|first=Phil|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-4789367.html|title=France are sent home by Kadlec|newspaper=[[The Independent]]|date=27 June 1996|access-date=12 January 2013|url-status=usurped|via=HighBeam Research|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130614235829/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-4789367.html|location=London, England|archive-date=14 June 2013}}</ref> where he scored his nation's second penalty shot.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-4789360.html|title=Euro 96 Semi-finals|newspaper=[[The Independent]]|date=27 June 1996|access-date=12 January 2013|url-status=usurped|via=HighBeam Research|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130604004548/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-4789360.html|location=London, England|archive-date=4 June 2013}}</ref> He and the Czech Republic team lost 2–1 in the final to Germany, who scored a [[golden goal]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Vogts' triumph over adversity |first=Ken |last=Jones |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/vogts-triumph-over-adversity-1326840.html |website=[[The Independent]]|publisher=Independent Print Limited |date=1 July 1996 |access-date=19 June 2012 |archive-date=27 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190927095905/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/vogts-triumph-over-adversity-1326840.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Euro 2000 ===
Before [[UEFA Euro 2000|Euro 2000]], Nedvěd could not train normally due to an ankle injury.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/euro2000/teams/czech_rep/783499.stm|title=Czechs counting on Nedved's ankle|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=8 June 2000|access-date=2 January 2013|archive-date=3 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190203030420/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/teams/czech_rep/783499.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> The Czechs' first match (against the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]]) saw him and international teammate [[Jan Koller]] hit the [[Goal (sport)|woodwork]] without scoring, before the Dutch scored a controversial penalty to win 1–0.<ref name=bbceuro2000>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/teams/czech_rep/801500.stm|title=Republic Czech out|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=22 June 2000|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-date=13 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180813075415/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/teams/czech_rep/801500.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> In the second match, against France, he was fouled, where the resultant Czech penalty was converted by [[Karel Poborský]] to even the score at 1–1.<ref name=FranceCzech2000>{{cite web|url=http://en.archive.uefa.com/competitions/euro2012/history/season=2000/round=1458/match=64865/report=rp.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130105051122/http://en.archive.uefa.com/competitions/euro2012/history/season=2000/round=1458/match=64865/report=rp.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 January 2013|title=Henry fires down Czechs|publisher=UEFA|date=6 October 2003|access-date=2 January 2013}}</ref> Despite two shots on goal, Nedvěd could not beat French goalkeeper [[Fabien Barthez]] and France won the match 2–1.<ref name=FranceCzech2000/> Already eliminated after two matches, he played in the third group match, against Denmark; the Czechs achieved a 2–0 victory.<ref name=bbceuro2000/> After Euro 2000, Nedvěd took over the national team captaincy from [[Jiří Němec]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Filip|last=Saiver|url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/kapitan-trener-ma-jine-starosti-dnk-/fot_reprez.aspx?c=A010903_224757_fot_reprez_hdv|title=Kapitán? Trenér má jiné starosti...|trans-title=Captain? The manager has other worries...|website=[[Mladá fronta Dnes]]|location=Czech Republic|date=3 September 2001|access-date=2 January 2013|language=cs|archive-date=16 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170816061122/http://fotbal.idnes.cz/kapitan-trener-ma-jine-starosti-dnk-/fot_reprez.aspx?c=A010903_224757_fot_reprez_hdv|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Euro 2004===
Nedvěd was instrumental in the [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]] group stage match against the Netherlands. With two goals down after 19 minutes, he gave a man of the match performance as the Czechs rebounded to win 3–2.<ref>{{cite news|last=Hayes|first=Alex|title=Football {{!}} Euro 2004: Nedved masters Dutch in epic encounter|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-1861022.html|newspaper=[[The Independent]]|date=20 June 2004|access-date=1 January 2013|url-status=usurped|via=HighBeam Research|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130604004522/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-1861022.html|location=London, England|archive-date=4 June 2013}}</ref> Nine players, including Nedvěd, were rested for the group match against Germany, with the Czechs already qualified for the knockout stage.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/3787551.stm|title=Germany 1–2 Czech Rep|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=23 June 2004|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-date=24 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180124002307/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/3787551.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> He received a yellow card, upheld on appeal, in the quarter-final match against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]].<ref name=euro04yellow>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/czech_rep/3848561.stm|title=Nedved yellow card stands|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=29 June 2004|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-date=1 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190701223306/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/czech_rep/3848561.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> This meant Nedvěd would miss the final if he received another yellow card in the semi-final against [[Greece national football team|Greece]].<ref name=euro04yellow/> However, Greece defeated the Czechs, and Nedvěd came off as a substitute after a knee injury.<ref name=2004intlretirement>{{cite web |url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/worldcup/news/kind=1/newsid=238209.html|url-status=dead|title=Nedved calls time on Czech career|publisher=UEFA|date=24 September 2004|access-date=20 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041030211626/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/WorldCup/news/Kind=1/newsId=238209.html|archive-date=30 October 2004}}</ref> After their exit from the tournament, Nedvěd announced his retirement from the national team;<ref name=2004intlretirement/> he was named to the Team of the Tournament alongside countrymen [[Petr Čech]] and [[Milan Baroš]].<ref name="All-star squad revealed">{{Cite news|title=All-star squad revealed|url=http://www.euro2004.com/News/Kind=1/newsId=205742.html|publisher=UEFA|date=5 July 2004|access-date=5 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040707012523/http://www.euro2004.com/News/Kind=1/newsId=205742.html|archive-date=7 July 2004}}</ref>

===2006 World Cup===
[[File:Nedved - 2006 FIFA World Cup (cropped).jpg|thumb|Nedved captaining the Czech team in its final group stage match against [[Italy national football team|Italy]]]]
Nedvěd was persuaded by coach [[Karel Brückner]] and his teammates to come out of international retirement in time for the [[2006 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA play-off)|2006 World Cup qualification playoffs]] against [[Norway national football team|Norway]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/potvrzeno-v-kadru-pro-baraz-je-i-nedved-dyq-/fot_reprez.aspx?c=A051102_150823_fot_reprez_min|title=Potvrzeno: V kádru pro baráž je i Nedvěd|trans-title=Confirmed: Nedvěd also in the squad for the play-off|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|location=Prague|publisher=Mafra|date=2 November 2005|access-date=2 February 2012|language=cs|archive-date=6 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130606205429/http://fotbal.idnes.cz/potvrzeno-v-kadru-pro-baraz-je-i-nedved-dyq-/fot_reprez.aspx?c=A051102_150823_fot_reprez_min|url-status=live}}</ref> in which the Czech Republic qualified for the final tournament for the first time since the [[dissolution of Czechoslovakia]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Clarke|first=Gemma|url=http://football.guardian.co.uk/worldcup2006/minbymin/0,,1788308,00.html|title=Czech Republic 0–2 Ghana|website=The Guardian|date=17 June 2006|access-date=4 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060630163049/http://football.guardian.co.uk/worldcup2006/minbymin/0,,1788308,00.html|archive-date=30 June 2006}}</ref> Although Nedvěd's World Cup participation was jeopardised by a June knee injury,<ref>{{cite news|title=Nedved hurts knee during training|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/world_cup_2006/teams/czech_republic/5060552.stm|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=8 June 2006|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-date=2 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702173551/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2006/teams/czech_republic/5060552.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> he was able to play.

The Czechs won the first match of the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]] 3–0 against the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4852720.stm|title=USA 0–3 Czech Republic|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=12 June 2006|access-date=4 June 2013|archive-date=4 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190704093458/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4852720.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> but key players were injured. They later lost their next two group matches against [[Ghana national football team|Ghana]] and eventual winners Italy, finishing third in their group.<ref name=ghana2006>{{cite news|first=Jamie|last=Jackson|title=Gyan catches Czechs cold as Ghana gain a glimpse of brazil|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/jun/18/worldcup2006.match1|newspaper=The Guardian|date=18 June 2006|access-date=3 April 2015|archive-date=24 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221024200025/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/jun/18/worldcup2006.match1|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=italy2006>{{Cite news|title=Czech Republic 0–2 Italy|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4853358.stm|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=22 June 2006|access-date=2 February 2012|archive-date=22 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222162421/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4853358.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> Nedvěd's apparent goal at the beginning of the second half in the match against Ghana was ruled offside.<ref name=ghana2006/> His shots on goal against Italy were saved by Juventus teammate [[Gianluigi Buffon]].<ref name=italy2006/> Nedvěd again announced his retirement from the international scene before the August 2006 friendly match against [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]], in which he made his 91st and final appearance.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Nedved calls time on Czech career|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/internationals/4795429.stm|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=15 August 2006|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-date=7 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190707051721/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/4795429.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> He refused to reverse his decision before [[UEFA Euro 2008|Euro 2008]] despite requests from teammates and Brückner.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/archive/confederationscup/southafrica2009/news/newsid=744669.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129011829/http://www.fifa.com/tournaments/archive/confederationscup/southafrica2009/news/newsid=744669.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=29 November 2014|title=Čech urges Nedvěd to return|publisher=FIFA|date=17 April 2008|access-date=31 December 2012}}</ref> In total, Nedvěd made 91 appearances and scored 18 goals.

|access-date=29 February 2020 |archive-date=28 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250528141634/https://www.vice.com/en/article/the-cult-pavel-nedved/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="key">{{cite web |url=https://www.eurosport.co.uk/football/campionato-italiano/2003-2004/nedved-the-key_sto502012/story.shtml |title=Nedvěd the key|website=Eurosport|publisher=TNT Sports Media|date=1 November 2003 |access-date=29 February 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/oct/04/europeanfootball.sport |title=Anyone remember Paolo Negro? |newspaper=The Guardian |last=Richardson |first=James |date=4 October 2005 |access-date=29 February 2020 }}</ref> He was also an accurate [[Direct free kick|free-kick]] and [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty kick]] taker.<ref name=addio/>

Nedvěd was known for his trademark long blonde hair, which made him a highly recognisable player on the pitch,<ref name="haircut"/><ref name="cult"/> and was known for his tackling and work-rate, which allowed him to win possession of the ball and provide stability to the defenders.<ref name=furiaceca>{{cite web|url=http://www.radio.cz/en/section/czechstoday/pavel-nedved-a-truly-world-class-footballer-comes-into-his-own|title=Pavel Nedved – a truly world-class footballer comes into his own|work=[[Czech Radio]]|last=Velinger|first=Jan|date=29 October 2003|access-date=4 January 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130104131135/http://www.radio.cz/en/section/czechstoday/pavel-nedved-a-truly-world-class-footballer-comes-into-his-own|archive-date=4 January 2013}}</ref> His former Lazio boss [[Sven-Göran Eriksson]] described him as "an atypical midfielder, totally complete".<ref name="czech-cannon-pp">{{cite news |last=Donovan |first=Jeffrey |date=15 December 1999 |title='Cannon' Nedved aims for gold |url=http://www.praguepost.com/archivescontent/31248-cannon-nedved-aims-for-gold.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130104133009/http://www.praguepost.com/archivescontent/31248-cannon-nedved-aims-for-gold.html |archive-date=4 January 2013 |access-date=4 January 2013 |work=[[The Prague Post]]}}</ref> Despite his ability, Nedvěd's tenacious playing style and disciplinary record has been criticised by the football media, who accused him of being overly aggressive in his tackles; he has also been accused of [[Diving (association football)|diving]].<ref name="cult"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/2006/febbraio/13/Mancini_finale_nervi_tesi_Nedved_co_9_060213105.shtml|title=Mancini, finale a nervi tesi "Nedved è un simulatore Adesso pensiamo al Milan"|trans-title=Mancini, tense conclusion "Nedved is a diver Now we're looking to the match against Milan"|newspaper=Il Corriere della Sera|language=it|first=Matteo|last=Garioni|date=13 February 2006|access-date=12 December 2015|archive-date=22 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222110614/http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/2006/febbraio/13/Mancini_finale_nervi_tesi_Nedved_co_9_060213105.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Post-playing career ==
[[File:Football against poverty 2014 - Pavel Nedved.jpg|thumb|upright=0.85|Nedvěd in a 2014 charity match]]
Nedvěd ran the [[Prague Half Marathon]] in 2010 (his first marathon) and finished the course in a time of 1:49:44.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.iaaf.org/news/news/kenyan-double-in-prague-kosgei-defends-her-ti|title=Kenyan double in Prague... Kosgei defends her title|work=IAAF|date=27 March 2010|access-date=15 November 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141115153308/http://www.iaaf.org/news/news/kenyan-double-in-prague-kosgei-defends-her-ti|archive-date=15 November 2014}}</ref> He ran the 2012 [[Prague Marathon]] in a time of 3:50:02.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sport.idnes.cz/pavel-nedved-po-prazskem-maratonu-dr3-/atletika.aspx?c=A120513_213944_atletika_par|title=Nedvěd: Maraton mě vystresoval víc než penalta v semifinále Eura|language=cs|trans-title=Nedvěd: the marathon stressed me more than the penalty in the semifinal of the Euros|newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|location=Czech Republic|date=14 May 2012|access-date=3 June 2013|archive-date=8 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170708160024/http://sport.idnes.cz/pavel-nedved-po-prazskem-maratonu-dr3-/atletika.aspx?c=A120513_213944_atletika_par|url-status=live}}</ref>

Nedvěd was named International Personality at the 2012 [[FAI International Football Awards]] in February.<ref name="fai-awards">{{cite web|url=http://www.fai.ie/international/senior-men/102385-2012-three-fai-international-award-winners-announced.html|title=2012 Three FAI International Award Winners Announced|publisher=Football Association of Ireland|date=26 February 2012|access-date=31 December 2012|archive-date=29 November 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129193227/http://www.fai.ie/ireland/news/2012-three-fai-international-award-winners-announced|url-status=live}}</ref> In January 2013, he was banned from attending Serie A matches for three weeks after he insulted referee [[Paolo Valeri]] during Juventus' match against [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Digby|first=Adam|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1292205/juventus-board-member-pavel-nedved-banned-for-insulting-ref?cc=5739|title=Nedved banned for insulting ref|website=ESPN Soccernet|publisher=ESPN|date=8 January 2013|access-date=8 January 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130112173947/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1292205/juventus-board-member-pavel-nedved-banned-for-insulting-ref?cc=5739|archive-date=12 January 2013}}</ref>

===Directorship===
On 12 October 2010, [[Exor (company)|Exor]] (the [[Agnelli family]]'s investment company) nominated Nedvěd to be part of Juventus' [[board of directors]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/nedved-se-stal-clenem-predstavenstva-juventusu-turin-ppg-/fot_zahranici.aspx?c=A101027_165603_fot_zahranici_par|title=Nedvěd se stal členem představenstva Juventusu Turín|language=cs|trans-title=Nedvěd became a member of the board of directors at Juventus Turin|newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|location=Czech Republic|date=27 October 2010|access-date=4 January 2013|archive-date=31 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181031005348/https://fotbal.idnes.cz/nedved-se-stal-clenem-predstavenstva-juventusu-turin-ppg-/fot_zahranici.aspx?c=A101027_165603_fot_zahranici_par|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Board of Directors and Control Bodies – Profile: Pavel Nedved|url=http://www.juventus.com/en/club/investor-relations/corporate-governance/board-of-directors-and-control-bodies/|publisher=Juventus FC|access-date=23 April 2017|archive-date=9 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809011528/http://www.juventus.com/en/club/investor-relations/corporate-governance/board-of-directors-and-control-bodies/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 23 October 2015, Nedvěd was appointed vice chairman of the board of directors.<ref>{{cite news|title=Commitment, Passion, Brilliance: The Reasons Pavel Nedvěd Is so Loved at Juve|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2684270-commitment-passion-brilliance-the-reasons-pavel-nedved-is-so-loved-at-juve|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|publisher=[[TNT Sports Interactive]]|date=30 December 2016|first=Adam|last=Digby|archive-date=2 July 2019|access-date=23 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702222023/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2684270-commitment-passion-brilliance-the-reasons-pavel-nedved-is-so-loved-at-juve|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Company Profile: Juventus Football Club S.p.A.|url=http://www.borsaitaliana.it/companyprofile/pdf/en/546.pdf|website=[[Borsa Italiana]]|publisher=[[Euronext]]|date=16 June 2016|access-date=23 May 2017|archive-date=2 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702222034/https://www.borsaitaliana.it/companyprofile/pdf/en/546.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Nedved named Juventus vice president|url=http://www.juventus.com/en/news/news/2015/-pavel-nedved-named-juventus-vice-president.php|publisher=[[Juventus FC]]|date=23 October 2015|archive-date=17 August 2019|access-date=23 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190817000702/https://www.juventus.com/en/news/news/2015/-pavel-nedved-named-juventus-vice-president.php|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 28 November 2022, the entire Juventus board of directors resigned due to the ''Plusvalenza'' scandal, in which Juventus had committed capital gain violations.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/juventus-board-members-resign-in-massive-shock-andrea-agnelli-and-pavel-nedved-out-at-storied-serie-a-side/|website=[[CBS Sports]]|publisher=[[CBS]]|accessdate=30 November 2022 |date=29 November 2022 |title=Juventus board members resign in massive shock; Andrea Agnelli and Pavel Nedved out at storied Serie A side}}</ref> On 20 January 2023, Nedvěd was suspended from holding office in Italian football for eight months due to his involvement in the scandal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.figc.it/it/federazione/news/inchiesta-plusvalenze-accolto-il-ricorso-della-procura-15-punti-di-penalizzazione-alla-juventus/|title=Inchiesta Plusvalenze: accolto il ricorso della Procura, 15 punti di penalizzazione alla Juventus|trans-title=Capital Gains Investigation: Prosecutor's appeal accepted, Juventus penalized by 15 points|date=20 January 2023|access-date=20 January 2023|publisher=Italian Football Federation|language=it|archive-date=20 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230120203429/https://www.figc.it/it/federazione/news/inchiesta-plusvalenze-accolto-il-ricorso-della-procura-15-punti-di-penalizzazione-alla-juventus/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/juventus-penalized-15-points-from-serie-a-standings-11-execs-banned-for-mishandling-transfer-finances/#:~:text=Juventus%20have%20been%20handed%20a,(FIGC)%20announced%20on%20Friday.|title=Juventus penalized 15 points from Serie A standings; 11 execs banned for mishandling transfer finances|website=CBS Sport|publisher=CBS|date=20 January 2023|access-date=20 January 2023|archive-date=20 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230120235443/https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/juventus-penalized-15-points-from-serie-a-standings-11-execs-banned-for-mishandling-transfer-finances/#:~:text=Juventus%20have%20been%20handed%20a,(FIGC)%20announced%20on%20Friday.|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 8 January 2025, Nedvěd became sporting director of Saudi club [[Al Shabab FC (Riyadh)|Al Shabab]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport.cz/clanek/fotbal-nedved-byl-predstaven-jako-sportovni-reditel-saudskoarabskeho-klubu-as-sabab-5046173|title=Nedvěd byl představen jako sportovní ředitel saúdskoarabského klubu aš-Šabab|trans-title=Nedvěd was introduced as the sporting director of the Saudi Arabian club al-Shabab|date=8 January 2025|access-date=9 January 2025|publisher=Borgis|language=cs|website=Sport.cz|agency=[[Czech News Agency]]|archive-date=9 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250109062126/https://www.sport.cz/clanek/fotbal-nedved-byl-predstaven-jako-sportovni-reditel-saudskoarabskeho-klubu-as-sabab-5046173|url-status=live}}</ref>

As part of business group Fotbal HK 1905, Nedved will take control of the ownership of [[FC Hradec Králové]] as of 1 January 2026.<ref>{{cite news |first=Petr |last=Záleský |title=Hradecký fotbal kupuje skupina okolo Pavla Nedvěda. Fanoušci bouřili radostí |url=https://www.idnes.cz/hradec-kralove/zpravy/fotbal-fb-hradec-kralove-votroci-prodej-klub-nedved-ulich-springerova-zastupitelstvo.A251104_135113_hradec-zpravy_pos |newspaper=[[iDNES]] |date=4 November 2025 |access-date=17 June 2026 |language=cs}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Nedvěd started living with his wife Ivana in 1992.<ref>{{cite web |date=29 June 2006 |title=Jak rostou nové hvězdy fotbalu? |trans-title=How do the new stars of football grow? |url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/jak-rostou-nove-hvezdy-fotbalu-dm3-/fot_dsouteze.aspx?c=A060629_081028_fot_dsouteze_rou |access-date=4 March 2013 |work=Mladá fronta DNES |language=cs |location=Czech Republic |archive-date=5 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305015014/http://fotbal.idnes.cz/jak-rostou-nove-hvezdy-fotbalu-dm3-/fot_dsouteze.aspx?c=A060629_081028_fot_dsouteze_rou |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=family>{{cite web|last=Moravec|first=Martin|url=http://ona.idnes.cz/ivana-nedvedova-muj-zivot-s-pavlem-d5h-/spolecnost.aspx?c=A060615_134639_ona_ony_jup|title=Ivana Nedvědová: Můj život s Pavlem|language=cs|trans-title=Ivana Nedvědová: My life with Pavel|work=Mladá fronta DNES|location=Czech Republic|date=16 June 2006|access-date=4 January 2013|archive-date=15 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150915082902/http://ona.idnes.cz/ivana-nedvedova-muj-zivot-s-pavlem-d5h-/spolecnost.aspx?c=A060615_134639_ona_ony_jup|url-status=live}}</ref> The couple have two children who are named Ivana and Pavel after their parents.<ref name=family/> The couple split in 2019 and Nedvěd started dating an equestrian.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.blesk.cz/clanek/celebrity-ceske-celebrity/614976/fotbalista-pavel-nedved-46-krach-manzelstvi-ted-randi-s-blondynkou-luckou-23.html|title=Fotbalista Pavel Nedvěd (46): Krach manželství! Teď randí s blondýnkou Luckou (23)|language=cs|trans-title=Pavel Nedvěd (46): Family Separation! He now dates blond Lucie (23)|work=[[Blesk]]|location=Czech Republic|date=6 June 2019|access-date=6 August 2019|archive-date=7 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190807152531/https://www.blesk.cz/clanek/celebrity-ceske-celebrity/614976/fotbalista-pavel-nedved-46-krach-manzelstvi-ted-randi-s-blondynkou-luckou-23.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Nedvěd's 2010 autobiography was published in Italian as ''{{Lang|it|La mia vita normale. Di corsa tra rivoluzione, Europa e Pallone d'oro}}''. It was translated into [[Czech language|Czech]] as ''{{Lang|cs|Můj obyčejný život}}'' and released in the Czech Republic in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|first=Chuchma|last=Josef|url=http://zpravy.idnes.cz/jaka-je-knizni-zpoved-fotbalisty-pavla-nedveda-prumerna-p2e-/zpr_archiv.aspx?c=A110508_121118_kavarna_chu|title=Jaká je knižní zpověď fotbalisty Pavla Nedvěda? Průměrná|language=cs|trans-title=What is the book confession of footballer Pavel Nedvěd like? Average|work=[[Mladá fronta DNES]]|location=Czech Republic|date=8 May 2011|access-date=4 March 2014|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304092440/http://zpravy.idnes.cz/jaka-je-knizni-zpoved-fotbalisty-pavla-nedveda-prumerna-p2e-/zpr_archiv.aspx?c=A110508_121118_kavarna_chu|url-status=live}}</ref>
